# The CodeQL extraction guard fails on a jobs-API lag it could wait out

## Context

Three `CodeQL` workflow runs on 2026-10-23 failed in the `CodeQL extraction guard` job with the same message, while their `Analyze (javascript)` leg had completed successfully seconds earlier:

| Run | Head | Analyze (javascript) completed | Guard started | Guard read the jobs endpoint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [39915969169](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/39915969169) | `dev` abcfac68b4 | 07:14:52Z | 07:14:55Z | ≈07:15:01Z (+9 s) |
| [39916009057](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/39916009057) | `dev` 3317a124d9 | 07:13:32Z | 07:13:34Z | ≈07:13:39Z (+7 s) |
| [39916733521](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/39916733521) | PR #20032 09a84f2458 | 07:19:17Z | 07:19:38Z | 07:19:46Z (+29 s) |

Each log reads:

```
check-codeql-extraction: could not read an Analyze-leg log — refusing to certify clean from an unread surface.
  Analyze leg "Analyze (javascript)" is in_progress, not completed
##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.
```

The guard had passed on every run since 2026-10-22 23:38Z (eight runs). All three failed jobs were rerun after this diagnosis; the reruns read the same run's Analyze log once the endpoint had caught up.

Why it matters today: the v13.3.1 release PR (#20022, AC-5) must pass `dev`'s required checks including CodeQL. A guard red on that PR means a rerun or a ruleset bypass, the thing the two-phase release path (#19637) exists to avoid.

**Design authority:** the guard's own contract in `buildScripts/util/check-codeql-extraction.mjs`. Its fail-closed rule ("a single leg's fetch failure throws — an unread leg is an uncertified leg, never a silent pass") is kept in full. Its premise "A `needs: analyze` guard runs after all legs finish, so each leg's log is available" (docblock of `fetchAnalyzeJobLogs`) is what today's runs falsify at the Actions REST API's read time: the workflow engine had finished the leg, the `jobs` endpoint still said `in_progress`.

## The Problem

The `GET /repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{run}/jobs` view is eventually consistent. For 7, 9 and 29 seconds after the leg's recorded `completed_at`, it reported the leg as `in_progress`. The guard reads that view once ([`check-codeql-extraction.mjs:124-134`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/3317a124d9/buildScripts/util/check-codeql-extraction.mjs#L124-L134)) and throws on the first non-`completed` status. The bounded retry that #16088 added for the same class of race on the log fetch ([`:139-155`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/3317a124d9/buildScripts/util/check-codeql-extraction.mjs#L139-L155)) runs only after that check, so it never applies. The memory trail has the class on record: on 2026-07-27 the guard failed eight seconds after the leg completed, on the log fetch; #16075 → #16088 retried the log fetch; the status read in front of it stayed a single shot.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml:75-93`: `extraction-guard` with `needs: analyze`, `actions: read`, runs `node buildScripts/util/check-codeql-extraction.mjs`. The dependency is satisfied by the workflow engine; the guard then re-derives the leg's state from the REST view.
- `buildScripts/util/check-codeql-extraction.mjs`, `fetchAnalyzeJobLogs`: one jobs read → filter legs by name → `if (leg.status !== 'completed') throw` → per-leg log fetch with `retryDelays` (default `[1000, 2000, 4000]`) and `sleep` seams.
- `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/check-codeql-extraction.spec.mjs:228-239` pins today's behaviour as "an incomplete Analyze leg is terminal and never fetches its log". That arm encodes the false premise and turns around with the fix.

## The Fix

`buildScripts/util/check-codeql-extraction.mjs`, `fetchAnalyzeJobLogs`:

- While any matching leg is not `completed`, re-read the jobs endpoint on the same backoff seams (`sleep`, `retryDelays`); only an exhausted wait throws, naming the leg, its last status, the number of reads and the elapsed window, and no log is fetched for it. The log fetch then runs as today.
- Raise the default `retryDelays` to `[1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 32000]` (63 s bound) so the default covers the longest lag measured today (29 s) with margin; a CodeQL leg takes two to five minutes, so the bound costs CI nothing it notices. The docblock states the premise correctly: the engine has finished the leg, the REST view may trail it.
- Spec: replace the terminal arm with two: a leg reported `in_progress` on the first read and `completed` on the second is certified from its log after exactly one backoff (red on today's code); a leg that never reaches `completed` within the backoff stays fail-closed, names it, and never fetches its log.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Unit arm, red on `dev` 3317a124d9: jobs read 1 reports `Analyze (javascript)` as `in_progress`, read 2 as `completed`; `fetchAnalyzeJobLogs` resolves with the leg's log and the sleep seam recorded exactly the first delay.
- [ ] AC-2: Unit arm: every jobs read reports `in_progress`; the call rejects with a message naming the leg, the status `in_progress`, the number of reads and the elapsed milliseconds, and the log endpoint was never fetched.
- [ ] AC-3: The #16075 arms (transient 404 retried, terminal 403 immediate, 503 exhaustion fail-closed, malformed payload terminal) pass unchanged.
- [ ] AC-4: The default bound is stated in the docblock and exceeds 29 s, the longest lag measured in this ticket's Context.
- [ ] AC-5 (cut-side): the fix is on `dev` before the v13.3.1 release PR opens, so that PR's CodeQL run carries the patched guard; recorded on #20022.

## Out of Scope

The Analyze job and the CodeQL action; the alert gate (ruleset 19087298); the log parser (`findCodeqlExtractionErrors`); any `continue-on-error` on the guard job.

## Avoided Traps

- A fixed `sleep` step before the guard: guesses the lag, the `check-fixed-sleeps` class.
- `continue-on-error: true` on the guard job: turns a fail-closed gate into a silent pass, the exact failure #15370 was filed to stop.
- Reading the check-runs API instead of the jobs API: the same eventually consistent store.
- Folding the guard into the Analyze job as a final step: a job cannot read its own completed log while it runs.
